Subject: Scarlet Labs — Dedicated capacity sprint & token-flow worksheet

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Based on what you showed, I think a short focused capacity-sprint will get us to a confident Dedicated commitment without over-provisioning. Proposed scope: a two-week sizing run where we validate tokens/sec demands, p95/p99 latency fit versus your SLOs, and a recommended slab allocation (including headroom and optional shared-burst plan).

To get started I need the following from your side if possible:
- 14-day traffic export (minute granularity) with request_id, model_variant, input_tokens, output_tokens, timestamp (CSV is fine).
- Your target SLOs (p95 latency target, p99 if you track it), and acceptable tail-latency for the UI experience.
- Typical and peak prompt lengths (avg tokens, 50/90/99pct).
- Any expected campaign day spikes or scheduled batch jobs (dates/times).

Deliverables from our sprint:
1) Tokens/sec mapping to recommended slab (GPU count + type) at your target p95.
2) Headroom recommendation (percent reserve) and burst strategy.
3) Canary plan (traffic ramp steps and monitoring hooks).
4) A committed-slabs pricing sketch for the deal thread.

Timeline: we can turn the sprint around in 7 business days after we receive the data. Ben will do the initial throughput modeling; Lauren will own canary/ops checklist.

If you can drop the CSV and the model profile into the Drive link below I’ll kick off the sizing run.

Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/s/Scarlet/traffic-worksheet

Thanks,
David

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Scarlet Labs — Dedicated capacity sprint & token-flow worksheet

David / Lauren —

Thanks for the export, Sara (cc'd above). Quick modeling notes after a first-pass parse of the CSV and the profile:

Summary (first-pass estimates):
- Baseline steady tokens/sec (business hours median): ~3,000 t/s.
- Observed peak minute: ~5,300 t/s.
- Nightly batch peak: ~3,667 t/s (220k tokens/min).

Hardware assumptions we've used for these numbers: 
- Model: 8B quantized (sparse optimizations off).
- GPU reference: A10G-equivalent slab (our common Dedicated SKU).
- Per-GPU sustained capacity estimate (p95 <= 600ms, avg request ~600 tokens): ~1,300 tokens/sec (this includes conservative KV-cache hit assumptions and small batching).

Slab sizing (initial recommendation):
- Committed slab = 5 GPUs => sustained ~6,500 t/s (1,300 * 5).
- This covers median business-hour load (~3,000 t/s) with ~116% headroom (6,500 / 3,000 - 1 = 1.166).
- To cover observed peak minute (5,300 t/s) while keeping p95 buffer, add burst pool of 2 GPUs (on-demand) => effective peak capacity ~8,100 t/s.

Headroom recommendation: 40% buffer for unknown growth and scheduling jitter on peak minutes. We get that by applying a buffer on top of observed peaks and letting the burst pool absorb short spikes.

Canary & rollout notes:
- Day 0-2: route 10% traffic to Dedicated slab (read-only paths + small write quota). Monitor p95/p99 and token-usage heatmaps.
- Day 3-7: 10% -> 50% -> 75% in two steps with auto-fallback to Hosted if p95 > target for two consecutive 5-min windows.
- Full cutover at Day 10-14 after regression checks and one end-to-end failure drill.

Questions for sizing precision:
1) Are you able to provide the per-endpoint breakdown (chat vs. batch vs. embeddings)? The CSV is per-request but doesn't tag endpoint.
2) Can we get a 7-day sample of CPU-side pre/post-processing latency for the busiest endpoints? That helps refine p95 compute budget.

I'll pull a slab_proposal_v1.xlsx with the numbers and a pricing sketch.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Sara —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the detailed numbers. Based on Ben's model and the traffic profile you've provided, here's our proposed committed plan and the operational playbook for the deal: 

Proposed commitment:
- Committed Dedicated slab: 5 x A10G-equivalent GPUs (monthly reserved).
- Short-term burst pool: 2 x A10G-equivalent GPUs available on demand for minute-scale peaks.
- Expected steady capacity: ~6.5k tokens/sec (p95 <= 600ms, per Ben's conservative numbers).
- Effective peak capacity with burst: ~8.1k tokens/sec (covers your observed 5.3k t/s peak with ~50% headroom relative to peak).
- Headroom policy: Maintain ~40% reserved headroom for unknown burstiness and month-over-month growth; we monitor and recommend adjustment after canary.

Canary & SLA specifics:
- 30-day canary window (as requested): 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 14 days with daily regression checks.
- SLA target during canary: p95 <= 600ms for interactive endpoints; automatic rollback to Hosted in event of sustained violation.
- Observability: token-level cost/latency dashboards + per-route traces (we'll share links to dashboards).

Ops & runbook highlights:
- Warmup: KV prefix cache priming recommended 24 hours before full cutover to avoid token-warmup spikes.
- Fallbacks: automatic fallback to a 2x smaller model variant if p95 > target for 2 consecutive 5-min windows; this will be included in playbook and tested during canary.
- Incident communication: Pager on-call + weekly sync during canary.

Next steps:
1) I’ll upload the slab_proposal_v1.xlsx with the numeric model and a pricing sketch to the Drive link.
2) If this looks good, Sara, I’ll send a DocuSign for a provisional 3-month reserved term (cancellable within the 30-day canary).
3) Ops & Eng kickoff to schedule warmup and runbook review.

DocuSign (provisional): https://app.docusign.com/03/sign?token=abc123scarlet
Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/s/Scarlet/traffic-worksheet

If you want a slightly larger committed slab (e.g., 6 GPUs) we can reduce burst-on-demand usage and increase steady-state unit economics — happy to walk through that trade-off on a quick call.

Thanks —
David
